name: Prototype
intent: Create new objects by copying an existing, pre-configured one instead of building from scratch.
scenario: A game spawns many goblins. A configured goblin (health, weapon list) is kept as a prototype, and every spawn is a clone of it.
problem: Building each enemy from scratch repeats setup code and can be expensive. Copying with a quick spread or assignment is tempting, but that is a shallow copy: the list of items is shared, so giving one goblin a shield gives it to all of them.
solution: Give objects a clone() method that knows how to copy itself properly, including nested data. Keep configured prototypes in a registry and spawn by cloning. The client never needs the concrete class or the setup details.
pain: Setup code is repeated for every goblin
A quick shallow copy shares the items list between goblins
Changing one clone secretly changes the others
Client must know how to build each enemy type
benefits: Spawning is just clone(): no setup repeated
clone() copies nested data, so clones are independent
New enemy types are new prototypes in a registry, no new code paths
Client depends only on the clone interface
whenToUse: Creating an object is costly or complicated, but copying a configured one is cheap
You need many objects that differ only slightly from a template
You want to create objects without knowing their concrete class
whenNotToUse: Objects are simple: just call the constructor
Objects hold resources that cannot be copied (open files, sockets)
Circular references make deep copying tricky
pitfalls: Shallow vs deep copy: forgetting to copy nested objects is the classic bug
Cloning objects with external resources (connections, handles)
Circular references can make clone() loop forever
Subclasses must remember to override clone() or they produce the wrong type

roles.label: Concrete Prototype
roles.description: Implements clone() with a correct, deep copy.

roles.label: Client
roles.description: Keeps a registry of prototypes and clones them on demand.

quiz.question: A game spawns goblins by copying a configured goblin field by field with a quick object copy. Each goblin has a name, a health number and a list of items. After one spawned goblin picks up a shield, every goblin in the level shows the shield. What is the most likely cause?
options: The health number is shared between copies, so the shield bonus was applied to the common value in every goblin
The copy is shallow, so all goblins point at the same items list and a change through one is seen by all
The registry hands out the stored prototype itself on every spawn instead of creating a second object
The copy ran before the items list was filled in, so every goblin received an empty list by reference
quiz.explanation: A shallow copy duplicates the references, not the list behind them, so all goblins mutate one list. Plain numbers are copied by value, so health is not shared. A registry that returned the same object would also share everything, but the symptom here is only the nested list.

quiz.question: A reporting service builds a Report by loading a template, querying lookup tables and applying styles, about 2 seconds each time. It needs 500 variants per hour that differ only in title and date range. Which approach fits best?
options: Make Report a singleton and change its title and dates before every export
Build each report in its own thread so the 2 second setup runs in parallel for all variants
Keep one fully configured Report and clone it, deep-copying mutable parts, then set title and dates
Subclass Report once per variant so each variant keeps its own constructor logic
quiz.explanation: The expensive setup is identical, and copying a configured object is cheap, which is the case for Prototype. A singleton would let concurrent exports overwrite each other. Threads and subclasses still repeat the 2 second setup 500 times.

quiz.question: A Session object holds an open network socket and a list of child Request objects, and each Request keeps a link back to its Session. A developer implements clone() as a recursive deep copy of every field. What goes wrong, and what is the right fix?
options: The clone must track already-copied objects to survive the cycle, and must open its own socket instead of copying the handle
The recursion ends safely on the cycle, so only the socket needs a fix, by sharing it between both sessions
The cycle makes deep copying impossible, so the pattern should be dropped and fields assigned one by one
The cycle is harmless, but the socket should be closed in the original before the copy is made
quiz.explanation: Blindly following the Request to Session link loops forever, so a deep copy needs a map of objects already copied. A socket is an external resource that cannot be duplicated by copying fields, so the clone should acquire its own. Sharing one socket between two sessions would interleave their traffic.
